commitResults.messageTitle: Add JavaDoc header comments for all non-private classes and methods
Add find command to search task descriptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Locating a task currently means listing everything and reading it by
eye, which gets slower as the list grows. The number that mark and
delete need can only be obtained the same way.

Add TaskList.find(), returning the tasks whose description contains a
keyword. It returns a new TaskList rather than printing, so the class
stays out of the display business and a search never disturbs the
original list.

Match case-insensitively and on substrings, so "Book" and "book" behave
alike and "sport" reaches "join sports club". A stricter match would
miss more than it caught.

Generalise showTaskList() to take a list and a heading so list and find
share one renderer, with numbering restarting at 1 for filtered results
to match what the user sees.

Javadoc and naming in the touched files are brought up to the SE-EDU
coding standard along the way; Ui and Storage still need the same pass.

processCommand had grown to 109 lines, more than three times the
30-line guideline and over twice the length of any other method here.
Length was the symptom; mixed abstraction was the cause. Deciding
which command was typed sat in the same method as the string surgery
each command needs, so a reader looking for the dispatch logic had to
scroll past index arithmetic and /by and /from splitting to find it.

Give each command its own handler and leave processCommand doing one
job: mapping a command word to the method that handles it. The switch
now reads as a table of contents for the class, and every method in
Nova is under 23 lines.

Three things follow from the split:

- The add commands repeated the same store-report-save line verbatim.
  Once the handlers were separated that duplication was obvious, and
  it moved into addTask().

- The names b, f and t are gone. They held the results of splitting on
  /by, /from and /to, and only made sense while the reader had the
  surrounding case branch in view.

- mark and delete still word their errors differently, so their
  validation was left separate. Unifying it would change what users
  see, which is a behaviour change rather than a refactoring and
  belongs in its own commit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the save-file field positions in Parser
commitResults.messageBody:
parseDataLine was the longest method left at 47 lines, but its real
problem was the bare array indices. A reader had to reconstruct the
save-file layout from scattered literals: [0], [1] and [2] for the
shared fields, then [3] and [4] for the type-specific ones. Worst of
all, [3] is the "by" date for a deadline and the "from" date for an
event, so the same expression meant two different things depending on
which branch you were reading.

The length checks were equally opaque. Three unrelated thresholds of
3, 4 and 5 each encoded "this type needs this many fields", stated
nowhere.

Name the positions as FIELD_ constants and split the type-specific
work into parseSavedDeadline and parseSavedEvent. FIELD_DEADLINE_BY
and FIELD_EVENT_FROM are both 3 on purpose: sharing a value is what
makes it explicit that the slot carries a different meaning per type,
which an unlabelled [3] hid.

With the positions named, every length check becomes the same
question, "does the field I am about to read exist", so the separate
count thresholds are no longer needed. Rename dataLineComponents to
fields and taskStored to description while the code is open, since
neither name said what it held.

Verified behaviour-preserving: 25 valid and malformed lines produce
identical results through the old and new parser, and loading a
corrupt save file end to end skips the same lines and recovers the
same tasks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace marker splitting with a guarded helper
commitResults.messageBody:
handleEvent decided whether its argument was well formed with a five
clause condition spanning two arrays and their indices. Reading it
meant holding all five checks in mind at once to work out which kinds
of input the command rejects.

It also built a throwaway empty array purely so the next line could
length check it. That existed only because the /to split ran before
the /from split was known to have succeeded, so something had to stand
in when there was nothing to split.

Split on one marker at a time and return early when a split fails, so
the empty array is no longer needed and each failure is checked where
it happens. handleDeadline had the same split and validate shape
written out longhand, so both now call the same helper.

Return the halves as a MarkerParts record rather than a String array.
An array would put the reader back to decoding parts[0] and parts[1],
which is the problem the previous commit removed from Parser; before()
and after() say which half is which at every call site.

Verified behaviour-preserving: 28 deadline and event inputs, covering
missing markers, blank halves, markers inside descriptions and
repeated markers, produce identical output and an identical saved
file before and after.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move command argument parsing into Parser
commitResults.messageBody:
Nova had grown to 419 lines across 22 methods, more than three times
the next largest class. The earlier refactorings in this branch made
its methods short but left every one of them in the same class, so it
now handles wiring, the console loop, the GUI entry points, dispatch,
all eight commands, argument parsing, saving and message wording.

Parser already claims this work. Its header says it turns into values
both what the user types at the prompt and what was written to the
data file, yet the splitting of /by, /from and /to sat in Nova while
Parser handled only dates and saved lines.

Move splitOnMarker and MarkerParts to Parser. Both were already static
and read no Nova state, so nothing about how they behave changes; only
which class they belong to.

MarkerParts becomes a top-level record rather than a nested one. It
was private to Nova, which was right while Nova was its only user, but
a type shared by two classes cannot stay private. Package private
keeps it out of reach of anything outside nova.

Verified behaviour-preserving: the 28 deadline and event inputs and
the 23 command inputs used in the previous commits produce identical
output and an identical saved file before and after.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use a stream to filter tasks in find
commitResults.messageBody:
find declared an empty list, looped over every task, and added the ones
whose description matched. That is the shape streams exist to replace:
five lines of accumulate-as-you-go mechanics around one line of actual
intent.

Express it as a filter and a collect, so the method states what makes a
task a match rather than how the matches are gathered.

Collect with toCollection(ArrayList::new) rather than toList(). The
result is wrapped in a TaskList, which adds to and removes from the
list it is handed, and toList() returns an immutable list, so a later
add to a search result would throw UnsupportedOperationException.
Add assertions
Branch a code quality
Branch a streams

commitResults.messageTitle: Refuse to add events that clash with existing ones
commitResults.messageBody:
Nova accepted any event regardless of what was already scheduled, so a
user could double-book a time and only discover it by reading the list
back. There was no validation on the range either, so an event could
end before it started.

Refuse an event that overlaps one already in the list, naming every
event it conflicts with, and let the user override with a trailing
/force when the double-booking is deliberate. A marker was chosen over
a yes/no prompt because getResponse() answers one line at a time with
no memory between calls; a prompt would have made the chatbot modal and
behave differently in the console and the GUI.

Only events take part. A todo has no time at all, and a deadline is a
single instant rather than a span, so neither can meaningfully occupy
a period that something else also occupies.

Compare ranges as half-open, so an event ending at 4pm does not clash
with one starting at 4pm: back-to-back scheduling is normal and should
not be flagged. Skip events already marked done, since finished work no
longer holds the time.

Guard the comparison against zero-length events. Such an event covers
no time and so overlaps nothing, but the usual two-comparison overlap
test reports a clash when a zero-length instant falls inside another
event's span, because that test assumes both ranges are non-empty.

Reject an event whose range runs backwards, and treat a backwards range
in the save file as a corrupt line so it is skipped and counted with
the others. /force does not override this: a backwards range is invalid
rather than merely inconvenient, and there is nothing sensible to
compare it against.

Report at startup when the saved list already contains clashes. The
notices now come from getStartupNotices() rather than being printed
inline by run(), so the GUI can show them too. This also means the GUI
finally shows the unreadable-file and skipped-lines notices, which it
had been dropping silently.

commitResults.messageTitle: Style the user and Nova sides of the GUI differently
commitResults.messageBody:
The GUI still used the tutorial's layout, where both speakers were the
same HBox of a 99px avatar beside a label, merely mirrored. That framing
suits a conversation between two people, but this one is between a
person and an application, and the two sides carry different kinds of
content.

A user message is now a compact tinted bubble on the right with no
avatar, since a portrait of yourself conveys nothing. A Nova reply is a
full-width panel on the left in a fixed-width font, marked with an
accent stripe and the app's badge. The fixed-width font is not merely
decoration: a numbered task list only lines up in columns if every
character is the same width.

Move the colours into a stylesheet, and replace the absolute layout
coordinates with VBox and HBox so the window can be resized. Delete
User.png, which nothing references now.

Name only logical font families in the stylesheet. JavaFX does not
support the comma-separated fallback lists web CSS allows: it reads the
whole list as one family name, fails to match it, and falls back to
System without reporting anything.

commitResults.messageTitle: Trim GUI chrome so long replies get more of the window
commitResults.messageBody:
The window is expected to occupy a small part of the screen while a
reply can run to many lines, so space spent on decoration is space
taken from text. Three things were spending it.

The avatar cost 43px of width beside every reply, a permanent gutter
that could never hold text, and repeated one badge down the whole
conversation. Show it as the window icon instead, where the window
manager draws it once and the layout pays nothing.

The card around each reply cost a border, a shadow and inner padding on
all four sides to draw a box the eye did not need, since the rule down
the left already marks who is speaking. Set replies on the page.

Padding and font sizes throughout were chosen for a comfortable desktop
window rather than a narrow one. Tighten them, and deepen the bubble
blue, which at 3.45:1 against white text fell short of the 4.5:1 needed
at this size; it now measures 4.83:1.

On the same conversation in a 400px window the transcript is 539px tall
rather than 744px, and a reply is laid out across 382px rather than
317px. Lower the minimum window width to 320 to suit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for storage, command dispatch and message text
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage and Nova had no tests at all, which left the file format and
every command's error handling uncovered -- 568 lines including the
place where all command behaviour lives. Parser, Task and TaskList were
tested only where a bug had previously been found.

Add StorageTest, NovaTest and UiTest, and extend the three existing
classes, taking the suite from 34 tests to 178.

Split the assertions by concern: UiTest pins the exact wording, while
NovaTest asserts behaviour and resulting state. Rewording a message then
breaks one test rather than thirty, while a change in behaviour still
breaks several.

Point every test at a JUnit temporary directory, so no test can read or
overwrite the real data file.

Verified the suite by mutating the source eleven times, including the
three bugs this project has actually hit: events saved under the
deadline letter, edits lost because saving appended rather than
rewrote, and impossible dates quietly moved by lenient resolving. All
eleven were caught.
